rationale_bullets: The Sorsby plan died in June - his college career ended amid the legal battle (P6, printed post-resolution; the flag from the Cincinnati build, verified here). He was the #2 transfer QB; he is not a rating input.

Will Hammond (78.8/129) is the guy: Top200 pedigree, career 1,151/9 across 2 starts plus relief (won the Utah 4Q in relief, 2 rush TD vs Kansas, 64-yd run), dual-threat - and an ACL rehab with a 'full return in mid-August, just in time for kickoff' (P6).
Kirk Francis (58.0/98 in '25; 3,045/18-13 career at Tulsa) is real-starts insurance with weak recent tape; Lloyd Jones III (PS#39) develops behind.
50 = average: high-quality small-sample tape and elite surroundings against ACL timing and two career starts. PS pre-resolution: 'fine year if he is the starter.'
Both All-B12 sophomores return: Dickey (76.0; 1,124 at 5.4, 1st-team B12, 263 vs Kansas) and Williams (88.4; 868 at 5.6 plus 371 receiving as the team's #5 receiver and a 99-yd KR TD).
Joyner (USC 4* transfer; 478 at 7.6 in '24) is back healthy behind them - 'somehow they retained all three' (P6); PS calls it his #7 RB corps nationally.
72, H: two proven P4 all-league backs plus blue-chip depth; H because tape, feeds, and all three books agree completely.
The inside is elite: TE Carter (82.2; 624, 2nd-team B12, 2nd among league TEs) returns with All-MW Carpenter (69.8; Nevada's leading receiver) added behind him.
Outside is a reload: Douglas (846) and Virgil (705) were both drafted; Eakin (67.4; 637) is the lone returning starter, with 5* Hudson (78.1/7 gm) carrying breakout framing.

The haul is P4-real: K.Johnson (69.0; 695 at Pitt, two-year starter), Simmons (71.2; 457 at 18.3 at Auburn, Top200), Lee (80.2; 589 at 18.4 Liberty), J.Jones (1,167 at 22.9, 1st-team SWAC); Top100 FR Campbell behind. 'Plenty of firepower here yet again' (P6).
62 = comfortably above average: depth and TE quality proven, top-line production new.
data_gaps: Target tree with a new QB
grades_detail.g5_guard_note: Lee (Liberty) and J.Jones (SWAC) tape G5/FCS-discounted; the 62 leans on Carter/Eakin/Johnson P4 tape

rationale_bullets: Three All-B12-caliber starters return: Sampson (71.8/926; 3rd-team B12 LT), Ponton (69.2/942; 14 starts at RT), Wilson (66.4/962; 27 starts at C) - from a line that was 84th-pctile pass-block/70th run-block.

The guard pair re-forms: 2nd-team B12 Carter (70.8/949) and Jados left; Church (65.1/514; Louisville 4*-transfer) and Zambrano (25 FCS starts) step in with 5* Ojo, Top100 Gilmore, and Upshaw (PS#50) as the young wave - 'deepest OLine' of the McGuire era (PS).
P6's honest read of '25: 'strong enough to win the conference, but on the Playoff tier a limiting factor' (#60 Run Push, #51 Pass Pro; 1 ypc and 4 sacks vs Oregon).
60 = above average: three proven P4 tackles/center, interior projection.

The '25 line (68 rush ypg at 2.2, 41 sacks; RDEF and PRSH both 99th pctile) lost four drafted starters: Bailey (93.3; 1st-team AA, 14.5 sk), Height (92.5; 10 sk), Hunter (80.4; 2nd-team AA), Gill-Howard.
What stays is real: Holmes (85.3/564; 3rd-team B12, 9 TFL - the best returning tape) and Cofield (73.8/287).

The reload is curated, G5-heavy: Trick (91.3/671; 1st-team MAC, 8.5 sk), White (82.9/642; 19.5 sk over two SDSU years), Mathis (84.5/453; 2nd-team MAC), Ibirogba (77.3/395; top-rated 4* transfer from Wake), Laventure (76.1/657; 10.5 TFL), Butler (74.0/305 UW), plus 5* FR Guyton. McGuire: Trick/Holmes/White are 'next year's NFL draft picks.'
65 = clearly above average, not the '25 monster - PS's 'figure to be less dominant' is the sober read.
grades_detail.g5_guard_note: Trick 91.3 / White 82.9 / Mathis 84.5 earned vs MAC/MW; guard holds the unit at 65 vs the proxy's 85

rationale_bullets: The Butkus winner is gone: Rodriguez (93.0/772; 117 tkl, 11 TFL, 7 FF, 4 INT, unanimous AA, 5th in the Heisman) - P6 calls him irreplaceable, and he is.

But the duo that remains is the best returning-tape LB pair graded this round: Roberts (86.3/791; 3rd-team B12, 90 tkl, B12 title-game MVP with 2 INTs) + Romaine (76.5/517; two-time All-B12 at Kansas State, the #2 LB transfer).
Platt (67.9/357; 40 tkl at Houston - '25 tape real despite P6's stale injury line) and Golwas (71.7/99) give depth; 'they remain strong but will miss their Heisman contending LB' (PS).
62 = solidly above average on two proven P4 all-league starters.
data_gaps: Rodriguez's takeaway production (7 FF/4 INT) irreplaceable

rationale_bullets: Four starters return from a 99th-pctile coverage unit (#8 PDR), three with 80+ tape: Pollock (82.5/797; 1st-team B12, 13 pd, 5 INT - 'high NFL DC next year'), Jordan (82.3/794; 14 st FS), Curry (80.9/745; 14 st STAR, #4 tackler), plus Boyd (73.4/528; 9 pd).
The one opening goes to Morgan (71.5/113; Top200 'spring hero and ballhawk'), and the depth tape is real: Hampton (82.7/97), Balfour (72.2/334).
The loss is the drafted FS Wisniewski (83.9/808; #3 tackler); PS: 'remains strong… will probably drop some.'
70, H = just under the WSU-DB-72 exemplar: three 80+ returning starters; H on tape/source unanimity.
Harrington returns as a Groza semifinalist and 1st-team All-B12: 22-28 with a 58-long, 41-42 PAT, 76 touchbacks on 103 kickoffs.
The return and block units were elite: J'Koby's 99-yd KR TD, five blocked punts, 95th-pctile SPEC (PS's #2 STR season, their magazine-era high).
The only loss is P Burgess (43.5/40.4 net); Karoll (UCLA/Tulane vet: 43.5 avg but 36.7 team net LY) is a modest step down on tape. PS projects a '5th straight top 25 finish.'
65 = solidly above average: elite kicker + return game, new punter and regression-from-#2 priced in.
